ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Preventive Visit — Wilma Rudolph

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Ms. Rudolph is a 54-year-old hospital executive and former Olympic sprinter with an IDH-wildtype, MGMT-methylated glioblastoma of the left frontal lobe, treated with gross total resection and six weeks of radiotherapy with daily temozolomide, who comes for her yearly preventive visit on day 21 of her first adjuvant temozolomide cycle. The MRI three weeks ago showed no progression. She took the five doses of temozolomide without vomiting, using ondansetron before each. She wears the tumor-treating fields device about 19 hours a day; the scalp under the arrays is a little pink but not broken. She is tired by mid-afternoon but works mornings from home. She has had no headache, seizure, change in speech, weakness or fall. Her right hand is back to normal for writing. She walks most days with the cane she keeps for uneven ground. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-29; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 66.9 kg; blood pressure 118/72; pulse 76; temperature 36.5 °C
Craniotomy incision healed; hair loss over the radiation field; scalp under the arrays mildly pink, intact
Clinical breast examination with a chaperone, at her choice: no masses, skin or nipple changes, or axillary nodes
No leg swelling; calves soft and non-tender; left calf slightly smaller than the right, as before
Fluent speech; strength full in all four limbs; steady gait; Timed Up and Go 9 seconds

Three weeks of headaches on waking, with ten days of pauses in finding words and clumsiness of the right hand, in a previously well woman of 54: an intracranial lesion must be excluded. MRI of the brain with and without contrast booked for tomorrow morning, and neuro-oncology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem; no symptom of her real illness was made public. Superseded when the MRI showed a brain mass.

Left posterior frontal ring-enhancing mass, 3.8 cm, with central necrosis, surrounding edema and 5 mm midline shift, next to the language and motor areas; presumed high-grade glioma, with no primary cancer elsewhere on CT; tissue diagnosis pending
S — Synthetic imaging diagnosis before surgery; superseded by the pathology.

Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4, left posterior frontal lobe, MGMT promoter methylated, after gross total resection of the enhancing tumor; synthetic modern detail linked to her publicly reported brain cancer
S — Synthetic histology, molecular result and location; brain cancer is documented as the cause of her death (D), and nothing more about it was made public.

Late effects of childhood poliomyelitis: paralysis of the left leg in early childhood, treated with a metal brace, a special shoe, massage and heat, with full recovery of walking by about age 12 and a later career as an Olympic sprinter; no new weakness, fatigue or pain now to suggest post-polio syndrome
S — Documented childhood polio (D); the current absence of new symptoms is synthetic.
Vasogenic cerebral edema around the left frontal mass, with 5 mm midline shift, causing headache and contributing to the language and right-hand symptoms; treated with dexamethasone
S — Synthetic finding on the first MRI.
Steroid-induced hyperglycemia on dexamethasone: random glucose 168 mg/dL, with an A1c of 5.6% before steroids
S — Synthetic common effect of dexamethasone; resolved after the taper.
Lymphopenia from temozolomide, grade 2 (absolute lymphocytes 0.5 x 10^3/uL at the end of chemoradiation): Pneumocystis prophylaxis continues until recovery to grade 1 or better
S — Synthetic common effect of daily temozolomide with radiotherapy.

Periodic adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and the prevention plan updated. Her screening for breast, cervical and colorectal cancer is up to date, and we agreed to decide about the next rounds of screening together when they fall due, in light of her treatment. Influenza, PCV20 and the first recombinant zoster dose given today: inactivated vaccines are safe during temozolomide, though her response may be blunted. A COVID-19 vaccine this season is due at her pharmacy. She declined lipid screening for now while she is on treatment. [S]
Second zoster dose in one to two months.

Next preventive visit in one year.

Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4, MGMT methylated, on adjuvant temozolomide and tumor-treating fields (C71.1). Day-21 blood count: neutrophils 1.9 and platelets 121, both above the thresholds for the next cycle, so cycle 2 can start on day 29, and the dose can rise to 200 mg/m2 as the label allows when the cycle 1 nadir and tolerance are this good. ALT 33 and AST 29 U/L: the cycle 1 liver tests, drawn today with the count rather than at the midpoint of the cycle, are normal (the deviation is recorded in the cycle 1 note). Scalp redness under the arrays is grade 1. [S]
Cycle 2 of temozolomide at 200 mg/m2 on day 29 if counts are still adequate.
Topical corticosteroid cream for the scalp between array changes; shift the arrays slightly at each change.
Blood count weekly until counts recover, then on day 22 of each cycle.

Lymphopenia from temozolomide, grade 2 (D72.810). Absolute lymphocytes 0.6; Pneumocystis prophylaxis continues. [S]
Continue sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim three times a week.

Late effects of childhood poliomyelitis (B91). No new weakness, fatigue beyond what treatment explains, or pain in the legs to suggest post-polio syndrome; walking safely. [S]
Home exercises; check leg strength at each visit.

Follow-up: Cycle 2 of temozolomide on day 29 with a blood count first. Neuro-oncology review and MRI after cycle 2. Second zoster dose in one to two months; COVID-19 vaccine this season. Next preventive visit in one year. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with her consent, reviewing the advance directive she completed with the palliative care team last month. She wants treatment aimed at controlling the tumor for as long as it lets her live in a way she values, being at home and with the people she loves, and wants to be told plainly when that balance changes. Her named health care agent is recorded in the confidential part of the chart and is not named here. She asked that information about her health go only to the people she names. To be revisited at each MRI and if her illness changes. [S]
